The orchard gate had swollen shut during the rain. Fallen fruit lay against the bottom rail, and the grass beyond it carried a thin silver film of water. Quinn arrived with a basket of empty jars. Ivo had left a ladder beside the wall the previous afternoon, but its feet had sunk so deeply into the ground that nobody could safely climb it.

“The lower branches will give us enough,” said Quinn. She set the basket on a flat stone and pushed a sleeve above her wrist. A list from Eren was folded beneath the jars. There were more names on it than Quinn remembered from last autumn, and several addresses belonged to houses beyond the ridge. The long morning would have to stretch further than expected.

Ayo tested the gate with a shoulder. He stepped back when the hinge began to bend. “We should lift it before we push again,” replied Ayo. A wedge of sunlight crossed the wall while the two worked the heavy frame upward. At last the latch scraped free, scattering drops from the nearest leaves. The opening was just wide enough for a basket.

Quinn crossed first and examined the fruit beneath a low branch. “Leave the bruised ones in a separate pile.” She turned an apple in the light, following the shallow mark made by a bird. The skin was sound beneath it. Across the orchard, an old scarecrow leaned toward the hedge as if inspecting the same problem. Its coat had lost both buttons during the summer.

“The smaller jars should go to the far houses,” said Ayo. He held the gate while Quinn moved the baskets through. The path over the ridge was narrow, and the lighter parcels would be easier to carry. Neither wanted another broken jar on the stones above the stream. Last year the smell of cooked apples had lingered there for days.

Shortly after noon the first basket was full. Quinn placed the folded list on top, keeping the paper away from the damp grass. The names still made a long column, but the work now had a shape. Ayo eased the gate against its post without fastening it. The orchard would remain open until the last empty jar had found a place in a basket.
